```{r}
source(file.path('functions/fxn_read_milk_folder.R'))
source(file.path('functions/fxn_read_nedap_attentions.R'))

# GC's lame functions (fxn_collapse_lesions, fxn_trim_vars, fxn_dz_status) -
# fetched live from GitHub, same mechanism report_explore_lame_new.qmd uses.
# Two local overrides are sourced AFTER fxn_load_os_fxns() specifically so
# they win over the GitHub versions in the global environment:
#  - functions/fxn_code_lesions.R: the GitHub version's `trimonly` logic
#    only checks the *protocols* field for "NONE" - this farm's
#    routine/no-lesion trims are coded "NONE" in the *remark* field
#    instead, which the GitHub version doesn't check, so it silently
#    misclassifies every routine trim as having a lesion.
#  - functions/fxn_collapse_lesions.R: the GitHub version reassigns its
#    own `data` variable to an already-one-row-per-date subset before
#    computing the max() union across that date's lesion columns, so
#    when a cow has multiple event rows on the same date coding
#    DIFFERENT lesions, only whichever row survives the earlier
#    reduction keeps its lesion flags - the rest are silently dropped
#    (confirmed against a real cow with 4 same-day LAME rows: only 1 of
#    her 3 distinct lesion types survived under the GitHub version).
source(file.path('functions/fxn_load_os_fxns.R'))
fxn_load_os_fxns()
source(file.path('functions/fxn_code_lesions.R'))
source(file.path('functions/fxn_collapse_lesions.R'))

# Shared analysis functions: the cohort, exclusions and Q1-Q6 builds, so this
# report and the farm summary apply the same rules from one definition.
source(file.path('functions/fxn_nedlame_analysis.R'))

events_all <- read_parquet('data/intermediate_files/events_all_columns.parquet')
events_formatted <- read_parquet('data/intermediate_files/events_formatted.parquet')
animals <- read_parquet('data/intermediate_files/animals.parquet')
animal_lactations <- read_parquet('data/intermediate_files/animal_lactations.parquet')

date_max_pull <- max(events_all$date_event, na.rm = TRUE)
farm_name <- unique(events_all$location_event)

# NEDLAME go-live date, per the DairyComp setup: enrollment protocols were
# only turned on starting ~June 1 2026, so no NEDLAME alert can exist
# before this regardless of how "missed" a case looks.
nedlame_start_date <- min(events_all$date_event[events_all$Event == "NEDLAME"], na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: milk-data

# data/milk/ is not wired into any existing pipeline script. Raw milk rows
# only carry a raw `id` (not the composite id_animal), so they're resolved
# to a specific animal-lactation by nearest-preceding date_fresh (see
# fxn_read_milk_folder.R for why a naive date_dry window isn't safe here).
# Only the window Q1 actually uses is read. The folder holds every milk day
# back to 2023, but the curves only span milk_window_pre days before an alert
# to milk_window_post days after, so reading the lot wastes ~26 s and then
# hands ~10x more rows than needed to the resolver, whose join costs far more
# than the read. Derived from the data rather than hard-coded, so it follows
# the alert window and the params automatically.
milk_from <- min(cohort$first_nedlame_date, na.rm = TRUE) - params$milk_window_pre
milk_to   <- max(cohort$first_nedlame_date, na.rm = TRUE) + params$milk_window_post

milk_long <- fxn_read_milk_folder(from = milk_from, to = milk_to)
milk_resolved <- fxn_resolve_milk_to_lactation(milk_long, animal_lactations)
```

```{r}
#| label: nedap-attentions-data

# Raw Nedap sensor export - what the SENSOR actually flagged, independent
# of whether that flag ever reached DairyComp as a NEDLAME event. Used in
# Q4 to split "NEDAP missed it" cases into true sensor misses vs pipeline
# losses (a real cowcard/Pulse cross-check first surfaced this pattern -
# see the plan doc's Round 8/10). This is a one-time export, not a live
# feed, so its coverage window is whatever was current when it was

attentions_raw <- fxn_read_nedap_attentions()
attentions_resolved <- fxn_resolve_nedap_to_lactation(attentions_raw, animal_lactations)

nedap_coverage_end <- max(attentions_resolved$attention_date, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: q4-build

invisible(list2env(fxn_build_q4(
  cohort = cohort, all_nedlame_cows = all_nedlame_cows, lame_data = lame_data,
  events_formatted = events_formatted, events_all = events_all,
  animal_lactations = animal_lactations, enrolled_ids = enrolled_ids,
  nedlame_start_date = nedlame_start_date, params = params), environment()))

# The pilot cohort and the cows it never enrolled answer different questions, and
# pooling them produces a herd-wide rate that is dominated by the second group:
# a cow outside the cohort has no NEDLAME by construction, so she is "missed"
# almost definitionally. Reported separately rather than combined.
in_pilot_case      <- q4$tx_group != "Never Alerted (Not in Pilot Cohort)"
n_cases_pilot      <- sum(in_pilot_case)
n_miss_pilot       <- sum(q4$is_miss &  in_pilot_case)
n_cases_unenrolled <- sum(!in_pilot_case)
n_miss_unenrolled  <- sum(q4$is_miss & !in_pilot_case)
n_caught_pilot     <- sum(q4$caught_by_nedap  &  in_pilot_case)
n_warned_pilot     <- sum(q4$warned_not_acted &  in_pilot_case)
# These three must exhaust the cohort. Without this the sentence below quoted
# herd-wide caught/warned counts against a cohort denominator: 240 + 26 + 3
# is 269, not 263.
stopifnot(n_caught_pilot + n_warned_pilot + n_miss_pilot == n_cases_pilot)
stopifnot(n_miss_pilot + n_miss_unenrolled == n_misses,
          n_cases_pilot + n_cases_unenrolled == nrow(q4))

# Median days from a cow's first alert to her first trim, by arm. Quoted in the
# misses section to make the point that the caught-versus-alerted-earlier split
# is largely a restatement of time to trimming - the intervention - rather than
# a measure of detection. Computed here so the prose cannot drift from it.
days_to_trim_by_arm <- cohort |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, tx_group, first_nedlame_date) |>
  left_join(trims_all, by = c("id_animal", "lact_number"),
            relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(trim_date >= first_nedlame_date) |>
  group_by(id_animal, lact_number, tx_group) |>
  summarize(d = min(as.numeric(trim_date - first_nedlame_date)), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(tx_group) |>
  summarize(med = median(d), .groups = "drop")
med_days_to_trim_tx  <- days_to_trim_by_arm$med[grepl("TX", days_to_trim_by_arm$tx_group)]
med_days_to_trim_ctl <- days_to_trim_by_arm$med[grepl("Control", days_to_trim_by_arm$tx_group)]
stopifnot(length(med_days_to_trim_tx) == 1L, length(med_days_to_trim_ctl) == 1L)

# The misses section states n_miss_unenrolled and then splits it using
# n_pipeline_loss and n_true_miss, which are computed over ALL misses. That is
# only the same split while no miss sits inside the cohort. It was not always:
# with the stale-lactation bug there were 3, and the section printed
# 119 + 194 = 313 under a stated total of 310. The arithmetic assertions above
# did not catch it, because both sums were individually true - they were just
# taken over different populations.
#
# So assert the condition the PROSE depends on, not one that happens to hold.
# If a cohort miss ever reappears, halt: the split needs restricting to the
# unenrolled cases (filter misses_in_coverage on tx_group) before it can be
# quoted against n_miss_unenrolled again.
if (n_miss_pilot != 0)
  stop("n_miss_pilot is ", n_miss_pilot, ", not 0. The misses section splits ",
       "n_miss_unenrolled (", n_miss_unenrolled, ") with the herd-wide ",
       "n_pipeline_loss / n_true_miss, which is only valid while every miss is ",
       "outside the cohort. Restrict that split to unenrolled cases before ",
       "quoting it.")
```

```{r}
#| label: q4-sensor-build

# Coverage is capped at nedap_coverage_end - the raw export is a one-time
# pull, not a live feed. The lookback window only looks BACKWARD from
# date_event, so a case is fully checkable as long as date_event itself
# is on/before the coverage end date; cases after that are flagged as
# "Not Checked" rather than silently miscounted as true misses just
# because we don't have sensor data that far out yet.
q4_sensor <- q4_group |>
  mutate(in_coverage = date_event <= nedap_coverage_end)

# Same pre-filter-before-join pattern used throughout this report:
# restrict candidates to the checkable subset FIRST, then join - a
# left_join on the full q4_sensor table followed by a filter would risk
# silently dropping the "Not Checked" rows instead of correctly keeping
# and labeling them.
sensor_hits <- q4_sensor |>
  filter(in_coverage) |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, lookback_days_used) |>
  left_join(attentions_resolved |> select(id_animal, lact_number, attention_date),
            by = c("id_animal", "lact_number"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(sensor_hit = !is.na(attention_date) &
           attention_date < date_event &
           attention_date >= date_event - lookback_days_used,
         # Any flag before the lesion at ALL, however far back. Without this the
         # residual category below was called "Never Flagged (True Miss)" while
         # being factually false for 161 of the 190 cases it labelled - they had
         # been flagged, just outside the window. A residual must not be named
         # for a cause it does not measure.
         sensor_hit_ever = !is.na(attention_date) & attention_date < date_event) |>
  group_by(id_animal, lact_number, date_event) |>
  summarize(sensor_fired_in_window = any(sensor_hit),
            sensor_fired_ever      = any(sensor_hit_ever), .groups = "drop")

q4_sensor <- q4_sensor |>
  left_join(sensor_hits, by = c("id_animal", "lact_number", "date_event")) |>
  mutate(
    # The strings in case_when() and in levels= must match EXACTLY or the
    # non-matching ones become NA and vanish from every count and plot.
    # Every name here states what was OBSERVED, not what it is taken to mean.
    # The old set asserted causes: "Caught in Time" conflated the camera flag
    # with the DairyComp alert, "no action taken" read as blame for what was
    # only an absent trim, and "Never Flagged (True Miss)" was the TRUE ~
    # residual wearing a causal name while being false for 85% of its rows.
    detection_group_3way = factor(case_when(
      !in_coverage ~ "No Data (Outside Coverage)",
      caught_by_nedap ~ "Alert Arrived in Time",
      warned_not_acted ~ "Alerted Earlier, No Trim Followed",
      sensor_fired_in_window ~ "Flagged, No Alert Raised",
      sensor_fired_ever ~ "Flagged Earlier, Outside the Window",
      TRUE ~ "No Flag Found"
    ), levels = c(
      "Alert Arrived in Time", "Alerted Earlier, No Trim Followed", "Flagged, No Alert Raised",
      "Flagged Earlier, Outside the Window", "No Flag Found", "No Data (Outside Coverage)"
    ))
  )

misses_in_coverage <- q4_sensor |> filter(in_coverage, is_miss)
n_pipeline_loss   <- sum(misses_in_coverage$detection_group_3way == "Flagged, No Alert Raised")
n_flagged_outside <- sum(misses_in_coverage$detection_group_3way == "Flagged Earlier, Outside the Window")
n_true_miss       <- sum(misses_in_coverage$detection_group_3way == "No Flag Found")
# These three split the misses on a string. Rename a level anywhere and the
# comparison quietly matches nothing: the counts go to zero, the page still
# renders, and the numbers just come out wrong. Happened in the farm report.
stopifnot(n_pipeline_loss + n_flagged_outside + n_true_miss == nrow(misses_in_coverage))
pct_pipeline_loss <- round(100 * n_pipeline_loss / nrow(misses_in_coverage), 1)
n_outside_coverage <- sum(!q4_sensor$in_coverage)
# Misses specifically that fall outside coverage - the figure that belongs
# next to nrow(misses_in_coverage). n_outside_coverage counts ALL lesion
# cases outside coverage (caught ones included), so quoting it alongside a
# miss-denominated number mixes two bases.
n_misses_outside_coverage <- sum(!q4_sensor$in_coverage & q4_sensor$is_miss)

# Sensitivity on is_completed. The raw export marks some attention episodes
# as not completed, and the loader does not filter them out, so an incomplete
# episode currently counts as the camera having flagged her. Rather than make
# that choice silently, re-run the same window test using only completed
# episodes and report how many pipeline losses depend on the incomplete ones.
sensor_hits_completed <- q4_sensor |>
  filter(in_coverage) |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, lookback_days_used) |>
  left_join(attentions_resolved |> filter(is_completed) |> select(id_animal, lact_number, attention_date),
            by = c("id_animal", "lact_number"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(sensor_hit = !is.na(attention_date) &
           attention_date < date_event &
           attention_date >= date_event - lookback_days_used) |>
  group_by(id_animal, lact_number, date_event) |>
  summarize(fired_completed = any(sensor_hit), .groups = "drop")

n_pipeline_loss_completed_only <- misses_in_coverage |>
  filter(detection_group_3way == "Flagged, No Alert Raised") |>
  left_join(sensor_hits_completed, by = c("id_animal", "lact_number", "date_event")) |>
  summarize(n = sum(coalesce(fired_completed, FALSE))) |>
  pull(n)
n_pipeline_loss_incomplete_only <- n_pipeline_loss - n_pipeline_loss_completed_only
n_attentions_incomplete <- sum(!attentions_resolved$is_completed, na.rm = TRUE)
```

# **The Bottom Line**

- **`r n_misses` of the `r nrow(q4)` cows** found with a lesion got no useful warning from the camera. That splits three ways, and only the last is the camera failing to see her:

  - **`r n_true_miss` had no camera flag of any kind** before the lesion. This is the camera's genuine blind spot, and it is much smaller than the miss count suggests.

    - Digital dermatitis is over-represented among them and white line under-represented.

      - This is not surprising considering the model being trained on locomotion scoring.

  - **`r n_flagged_outside` were flagged, but only more than `r params$q4_lookback_days` days before the lesion** - too far back to count as a warning about it. See @sec-lookback for why that window was chosen.

- A further **`r n_pipeline_loss` were flagged inside the window but no `NEDLAME` was raised.**

  - Most of that is the enrollment rules working as designed.

    - **`r n_pipeline_loss_genuine` are confirmed losses** between the camera and DairyComp.

    - This excludes the first lactation animals that stopped being entered in the SmartSight instance in August.

- Trimming off the alert (Trim Treatment (TX) group) found a lesion in **`r n_extra_lesion_cows` more cows** than the control approach.

  - `r pct_trimmed_tx`% of TX cows were trimmed against `r pct_trimmed_ctl`% of Control. Since the groups were randmomized the TX lesions were we can infer that that they were found earlier.

- **No clear difference in milk or culling over 30 days.** The milk curves slightly favour TX, but cow-to-cow variation dwarfs the group difference, and with `r n_culls` culls in total the study cannot answer the culling question either way.

- More longer term follow up is required to measure other outcomes such as repeat lesions and longer-run production.

- The pilot gave valuable insight for the proposed follow up study and details of that proposal will follow.

Each of these is developed below, with the checks behind it.

# Setup in DairyComp

For this study the follow things were created in DairyComp to handle the file data from NEDAP daily.

- A command to clear all filein items before new data was brought in as a workaround to deal with historical flag issues in the NEDAP files

- New NEDAP lame event with 3 protocols to flag cows and criteria to create them

  - Low (score \<30 today, no alarm in the last 90 days, not trimmed in last 90 days, not a cow with history of upper leg lameness)

    - ENTER EC=70\\P215 FOR LFTYP=30102 LMFLG=1 LMSV=1-30 DSNLM=90-1 FTDAT\<-90 UPLAM\<\>1
    - The exclusions were added to prevent excessive alarms for cows with know locomotion issues.

  - Low Declining (no alarm in the last 7 days, so a cow already alerted is not re-flagged, and not trimmed in last 28 days)

    - ENTER EC=70\\P214 FOR LFTYP=30101 LMFLG=1 DSNLM=7-1 FTDAT\<-28

  - Strong Decline (no alarm in the last 7 days, not trimmed in last 28 days); the second OR statement lets a cow who already has a Low alert still raise a Strong Decline

    - ENTER EC=70\\P213 FOR LFTYP=30100 LMFLG=1 (DSNLM=7-1 FTDAT\<-28)(FTDAT\<-28 %73.NDLAME.101\>LOW)

- Cows were added to trim list with a command that uses an existing item (MNFRS) that randomizes cows by lactation group.

  - Enter FTDAT=1.1.1 for MNFRS=1 %.70NEDLAME.101=TODAY

Above commands were all run daily around 5 am after NEDAP file in occurred.

```{r}
#| label: same-day-trim-check

# Cows whose FIRST alert is stamped on the SAME DATE as a trim. The 1-7 day
# exclusion above cannot see these: it tests `trim_date < first_nedlame_date`,
# so a same-day trim never triggers it.
#
# Whether the alert preceded the trim cannot be answered from the event date,
# because the NEDLAME carries the date the 05:00 command ran rather than the
# date the camera detected her. It CAN be answered from the raw export: the
# batch loads at ~05:00 and stamps the load day, so an alert dated D comes from
# an attention in (D-1 05:00, D 05:00] - all of which precede any trimming on D.
# Path taken from the loader default rather than hard-coded.
sd_trim <- cohort |>
  select(id_animal, id, lact_number, first_nedlame_date) |>
  left_join(trims_all, by = c('id_animal', 'lact_number'), relationship = 'many-to-many') |>
  group_by(id_animal, id, lact_number, first_nedlame_date) |>
  summarize(same_day = any(trim_date == first_nedlame_date, na.rm = TRUE),
            prior7   = any(trim_date < first_nedlame_date &
                           trim_date >= first_nedlame_date - params$post_trim_exclusion_days,
                           na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') |>
  filter(same_day, !prior7)
n_same_day_trim <- nrow(sd_trim)

sd_raw <- readr::read_csv(eval(formals(fxn_read_nedap_attentions)$file),
                          show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(id = as.character(animal_number),
         st = lubridate::with_tz(lubridate::as_datetime(start_time_utc, tz = 'UTC'),
                                 'America/Chicago'))
sd_gen <- sd_trim |>
  select(id, D = first_nedlame_date) |>
  left_join(sd_raw |> select(id, st), by = 'id', relationship = 'many-to-many') |>
  mutate(in_win = st > lubridate::as_datetime(paste0(D - 1, ' 05:00:00'), tz = 'America/Chicago') &
                  st <= lubridate::as_datetime(paste0(D, ' 05:00:00'), tz = 'America/Chicago')) |>
  group_by(id, D) |>
  summarize(traced = any(in_win, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
n_sd_traced   <- sum(sd_gen$traced)
n_sd_untraced <- sum(!sd_gen$traced)
stopifnot(n_sd_traced + n_sd_untraced == n_same_day_trim)

# The cows the raw export cannot place were checked by hand against the
# DairyComp command logs (data/logs, 8 Jun - 11 Sep). Those logs are a one-off
# manual pull and are gitignored, so the audit cannot be recomputed here - the
# findings are constants, fenced by the assertion below so the prose cannot
# drift away from the chunk above if the cohort changes.
n_sd_log_nolog   <- 1L   # alerted 4 Jun, before the logs begin on 8 Jun
n_sd_log_checked <- 16L  # NEDLAME entry located in the log for the alert date
stopifnot(n_sd_log_checked + n_sd_log_nolog == n_sd_untraced)

# Of ALL the same-day cows, how many had a staff locomotion check the day
# BEFORE the alert - i.e. she was already on the trim list and the camera is
# not what put her there. Computed from CHKLAME so it survives a re-render.
# This is NOT the quantity fxn_build_control_trim_drivers() reports: that one
# counts a CHKLAME falling BETWEEN the alert and a LATER trim, and only 2 of
# these cows appear in it at all.
n_sd_staff_first <- sd_trim |>
  left_join(events_formatted |> filter(event == 'CHKLAME') |>
              distinct(id_animal, chk_date = date_event),
            by = 'id_animal', relationship = 'many-to-many') |>
  group_by(id_animal) |>
  summarize(sf = any(as.numeric(first_nedlame_date - chk_date) == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = 'drop') |>
  summarize(n = sum(sf)) |> pull(n)
```

# Results

- `r nrow(first_nedlame)` cows received a `NEDLAME` alert between `r format(min(first_nedlame$first_nedlame_date))` and `r format(max(first_nedlame$first_nedlame_date))`

- The analysis stops at `r format(analysis_end)`, the last day the raw Nedap sensor export covers.

  - Follow-up extends past this data to allow following of trims, culls and milk records.

- `r n_excluded_post_trim` alerts on cows were excluded as alerts occurred after a recent hoof trimming (1-7 days). These were still coded in DairyComp as the farm imports hoof trimming data a few days after the actual hoof trimming date.

  - See @tbl-post-trim-exclusion-table. for details on these cows

- **`r n_same_day_trim` cows had their first alert stamped on the same date as a trim** based on DairyComp logs and raw NEDAP flag exports they were flagged before trimming and considered part of the cohorts

With above exclusions and conditions it resulted in

- `r n_tx` cows enrolled in the **TX (Trim)** arm (`MNFRS = 1`, automatically added to trim list after an alert)

- `r n_control` in the **Control** arm (`MNFRS = 2`, staff or routine trimming would have added her to the trim list.

**NOTE**: *No cow is counted more than once in any table below. Where this report looks for "the" trim, LAME diagnosis, staff check, or NEDLAME alert for a cow, it either uses her **first** qualifying occurrence in the relevant window or asks only whether at least one occurred. Therefore a cow flagged or diagnosed repeatedly isn't counted more than once. When a single trimming date has more than one distinct lesion type coded (e.g. white line disease and digital dermatitis found at the same trimming), each distinct type is kept; the same lesion type coded more than once on one day only counts once.*

```{r}
#| label: post-trim-followup-check

# The real evidence for the artifact reading: did anything ever come of
# these alerts? Computed rather than asserted - an earlier draft described
# this as "a separate check (not shown here)" and instead leaned on the
# share of decline-type alerts, which turns out to be just the cohort's
# base rate (see prose below) and therefore argues nothing either way.
excluded_followup <- cohort_excluded_post_trim |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, first_nedlame_date, date_lact_end) |>
  left_join(
    events_formatted |>
      filter(event %in% c("LAME", "FOOTRIM", "TRIM")) |>
      select(id_animal, lact_number, followup_date = date_event) |>
      distinct(),
    by = c("id_animal", "lact_number"), relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  mutate(is_followup = !is.na(followup_date) &
           followup_date > first_nedlame_date &
           followup_date <= date_lact_end) |>
  group_by(id_animal, lact_number) |>
  summarize(had_followup = any(is_followup), .groups = "drop")

n_excluded_no_followup <- sum(!excluded_followup$had_followup)
pct_excluded_no_followup <- round(100 * n_excluded_no_followup / nrow(excluded_followup), 0)

# Base-rate comparison, so the decline-share figure can be reported honestly.
pct_decline_excluded <- round(100 * mean(cohort_excluded_post_trim$alert_type %in% c("LOW DECLINE", "STRONG DECLINE")), 1)
pct_decline_cohort <- round(100 * mean(cohort$alert_type %in% c("LOW DECLINE", "STRONG DECLINE")), 1)
```

### Time to next trimming after alert

These time to event curves measure **protocol compliance**.

- For each cow we took the first trim after her first NEDLAME alert, censored at end of lactation or culling.

  - It is clear that most of the TX cows got trimmed within 7-10 days as designed.
  - The difference between the time to event with a lesion (@fig-q2-lesion-plot) illustrates how the TX group finds more cows with lesions.

In TX the trim is caused by the alert, so the curve shows how well the protocol was followed.

The Control curve does a different job: nothing there acts on the alert, so it shows when those cows were trimmed anyway due to either staff flagging them or a routine scheduled trimming.

- A breakdown of the staff-versus-routine split is in @tbl-trim-driver.

## By Alert Type

Decline cows mostly all get trimmed

```{r}
#| label: fig-q2-alert-type-plot
#| fig-height: 6

alert_levels <- c("LOW", "LOW DECLINE", "STRONG DECLINE")

# ggsurvfit only exposes a single combined `strata` column, so a KM plot
# faceted by alert_type is built manually: fit one survfit2() per
# alert level (skipping any level without both treatment arms
# represented) and stack the tidy() estimates before plotting.
fittable_alert_levels <- alert_levels |>
  keep(\(a) {
    d <- q2_any |> filter(alert_type == a)
    n_distinct(d$tx_group) == 2 && nrow(d) >= 10
  })

q2_alert_type_km_data <- fittable_alert_levels |>
  map(\(a) {
    d <- q2_any |> filter(alert_type == a)
    fit <- survfit2(Surv(days_to_event, event_occurred) ~ tx_group, data = d)
    broom::tidy(fit) |>
      mutate(
        tx_group = str_remove(strata, "^tx_group="),
        alert_type = a,
        risk = 1 - estimate,
        # survival's CI bounds flip when converted to risk (1 - survival):
        # the upper bound on survival becomes the LOWER bound on risk.
        risk_low = 1 - conf.high,
        risk_high = 1 - conf.low
      )
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(alert_type = factor(alert_type, levels = alert_levels))

skipped_alert_levels <- setdiff(alert_levels, fittable_alert_levels)

ggplot(q2_alert_type_km_data, aes(x = time, y = risk, color = tx_group, fill = tx_group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = risk_low, ymax = risk_high), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~alert_type) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Days After First NEDLAME Alert", y = "% With a Subsequent Trim/LAME Event",
       color = "Treatment Group", fill = "Treatment Group",
       caption = "Shaded band: 95% confidence interval from the Kaplan-Meier fit.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

`r if (length(skipped_alert_levels) > 0) paste0("*Alert type(s) omitted for insufficient data in one or both arms: ", paste(skipped_alert_levels, collapse = ", "), ".*")`
:::

### How many trims with no lesions?

The table below shows the number of cows who had a first NEDAP alert and were trimmed **but** did not have a lesion.

**Note:** *This table's population is only the number of cows in the `r nrow(cohort)`-cow NEDLAME cohort that were trimmed.*

```{r}
#| label: tbl-q2-trimonly-summary

q2_first_event_detail <- q2_any |>
  filter(event_occurred == 1) |>
  left_join(lame_data |> select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, event, trimonly),
            by = c("id_animal", "lact_number", "date_event"))

q2_trimonly_tab <- q2_first_event_detail |>
  group_by(tx_group) |>
  summarize(n = n(), n_trimonly = sum(trimonly, na.rm = TRUE), pct_trimonly = mean(trimonly, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = 'drop') |>
  bind_rows(
    q2_first_event_detail |> summarize(tx_group = 'Overall', n = n(), n_trimonly = sum(trimonly, na.rm = TRUE), pct_trimonly = mean(trimonly, na.rm = TRUE) * 100)
  )

# Title built from the cells beneath it. It used to be typed by hand and had
# already gone stale against a rebuild, quoting a range the table contradicted.
# level is 'TX (Trim)', not 'TX' - matching on 'TX' silently gave numeric(0)
tx_lvl <- setdiff(q2_trimonly_tab$tx_group, c('Control', 'Overall'))
stopifnot(length(tx_lvl) == 1)
pct_trimonly_tx  <- round(q2_trimonly_tab$pct_trimonly[q2_trimonly_tab$tx_group == tx_lvl], 1)
pct_trimonly_ctl <- round(q2_trimonly_tab$pct_trimonly[q2_trimonly_tab$tx_group == 'Control'], 1)
trimonly_title <- sprintf('%d-%d%% of Trims do not have a lesion',
                          floor(min(q2_trimonly_tab$pct_trimonly)), ceiling(max(q2_trimonly_tab$pct_trimonly)))

q2_trimonly_tab |>
  gt(rowname_col = 'tx_group') |>
  fmt_number(columns = pct_trimonly, decimals = 1) |>
  cols_label(n = 'N Cows with Trim', n_trimonly = 'No Lesion', pct_trimonly = '% Trim-Only') |>
  tab_header(title = trimonly_title)
```

In the Control arm a cow is trimmed if she is flagged by farms staff (CHKLAME) or she is due for her routine trimming. The table below shows that the majority of trims in the Control group were due to routine trimming as only **`r n_ctl_staff` (`r pct_ctl_staff`%)** had a `CHKLAME` event.

- The rate of lesions an time after an alert of the CHKLAME vs routine trimming differs
  - Staff-flagged trims found a lesion **`r pct_lesion_staff`%** of the time at a median **`r med_days_staff`**.
  - Routine trims found a lesion **`r pct_lesion_routine`%** of the time at a median of **`r med_days_routine`**.

## How many extra lesions did the Trim Treatment group find?

From the time to lesion curve above ( @fig-q2-lesion-plot) it is clear that TX found more cows.

- A lesion was found in `r n_lesion_tx` of the `r n_cows_tx` TX cows (`r pct_lesion_arm_tx`%)

- In trimmed Control cows that was `r n_lesion_ctl` of `r n_cows_ctl` (`r pct_lesion_arm_ctl`%).

Rate-adjusted for the unequal arms, that is **`r n_extra_lesion_cows` more cows with a lesion identified**.

**Note:** *the denominator: this is the **full arm** (`r n_cows_tx` and `r n_cows_ctl`), not the trimmed subset the no-lesion table uses (`r n_trimmed_tx` and `r n_trimmed_ctl`).*

## Milk Production After 1st NEDLAME Alert

```{r}
#| label: q1-build

invisible(list2env(fxn_build_q1(cohort, milk_resolved, params), environment()))
```

The figures below compare milk production between the treatment groups. Cows were assigned to TX or Control at enrollment.

- `r n_milk_cows` of the `r nrow(cohort)` cohort cows had at least one milk record after their alert and a usable pre-alert baseline.

- More cows are contributing data closer to the alert day compared to further away.

  - a cow needs `r params$milk_window_post` days of milk records after her alert to appear at day `r params$milk_window_post`, and only `r n_milk_day30` have that so far.

    - This means the numbers can still change as the remaining cows get to 30 days after alert.

Overall numerically there is an advantage to the trimmed group in milk production after an alert but there is a lot of variation (the shaded part around the solid line) so this is not something to put a lot of trust in.

**NOTE:** *Due to the fact that cows were at very different lactation stages when flagged milk production is not directly comparable across cows. Each cow's production is normalized to **% of her own pre-alert baseline** (mean production over the `r params$milk_baseline_days` days before the alert) before averaging by day and treatment group. This allow us to isolates the shape of the trend/recovery from each cow's absolute production level.*

## Influence of Lameness History

Lifetime lameness history is important confounder in lameness work and this section considers the impact of that in this pilot. Sample size becomes and issue in this and this is presented mainly to consider for possible future work.

### Lameness History Distribution at Enrollment

@fig-chronic shows the breakdown of **New** vs **Chronic** cows that were enrolled. Chronicity is based on a cow's **lifetime record** at her first NEDLAME alert. Data going back to 2021 was used to establish chronicity.

- More New cases were enrolled

```{r}
#| label: fig-chronic
#| fig-height: 4

cohort |>
  count(tx_group, history_group) |>
  group_by(tx_group) |>
  filter(history_group %in% c("New", "Chronic")) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(history_group = fct_relabel(history_group, \(x) str_wrap(x, width = 14))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = history_group, y = n, fill = tx_group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", round(pct, 0), "%)")),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "N Cows", fill = "Treatment Group",
       ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.9),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 15))
```

@fig-chronic-milk compares milk production across the lesion history types.

```{r}
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Days Relative to First NEDLAME Alert", y = "Milk Production (% of Baseline)",
       color = "Treatment Group", fill = "Treatment Group",
       caption = "Shaded band: ± 1 standard error of the mean (≈ 68%). Not a test of the difference between arms.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Time to culling is compared below. The curves sit close together, but only `r n_culls` cows were culled (`r n_culls_tx` TX, `r n_culls_ctl` Control).

That is too few to tell whether trimming off the alert changes culling, more cows and time is needed to answer that question.

## What cows were missed by the system?

**First, the cows the camera was actually watching.** Of the `r n_cases_pilot` lesion cases in the pilot cohort, **`r n_miss_pilot` were missed**: `r n_caught_pilot` had an alert arrive inside the window and `r n_warned_pilot` had one arrive earlier with no trim in between. Every cow in the cohort is there by having been alerted, so this is not a detection rate - it is the statement that once a cow was enrolled, a warning always existed.

**Do not read the caught-versus-earlier split as camera performance by arm.** It is closer to a restatement of time to trimming, which is the intervention itself: a TX cow is added to the trim list automatically and trimmed at a median of `r med_days_to_trim_tx` days against `r med_days_to_trim_ctl` for Control, so her lesion is *found* sooner and the gap between her alert and her diagnosis is short by construction. That gap is protocol compliance, not detection - the same distinction the trimming section draws.

The rest of this section is about the cows the pilot never enrolled. Every cow with a `LAME`-diagnosed lesion on or after `r params$history_after_date` not in the cohort is checked here, whether or not she was ever in the pilot. For each, the question is whether a `NEDLAME` alert had reached DairyComp before the lesion was found.

A "miss" means **no useful warning reached DairyComp before the lesion was found** - either the camera never flagged her, or it flagged her and the alert never arrived.

- This was `r n_miss_unenrolled` cows in the pilot study.

Using the raw camera flag export data, the breakdown of those missed cow is as follows.

1.  **`r n_pipeline_loss` the camera flagged her inside the window, but no `NEDLAME` was raised.** She met the sensor's criteria and never entered the study.

    1.  Whether that is a pipeline failure or the enrollment rules working is shown below.

2.  **`r n_flagged_outside` the camera flagged her, but only more than `r params$q4_lookback_days` days before the lesion.** None of these carried a `NEDLAME` at any point before the lesion either, so the camera was producing signal on them and none of it became an alert. They are not counted as warnings, because a flag that far back cannot be attributed to this lesion - see @sec-lookback.

3.  **`r n_true_miss` had no camera flag at all.** This is the only group the camera genuinely did not see.

### Why the warning window is `r params$q4_lookback_days` days {#sec-lookback}

**It is `r params$q4_lookback_days` days because that is the horizon DairyComp itself runs on.** The decline routes gate on `FTDAT<-28` - a cow trimmed inside 28 days cannot raise a decline alert - and the post-trim suppression in this report uses the same `r params$recent_trim_suppression_days` days. Matching the analysis window to the operational one means the report is asking the question the farm's own system is set up to answer, rather than imposing a number of its own.

**The headline does not depend on it.** `r n_misses` cows got no useful warning, and that figure is identical at a 14, 21, 28 or 45-day window. Widening the window moves a case from *alerted earlier* to *alert arrived in time* - both of which are warnings - so the count of cows who got neither cannot change. The `r n_true_miss` with no camera flag at all is likewise fixed. What the window does move is the split *within* those groups: how many misses are attributed to the pipeline rather than to a flag too old to count, and how many cohort alerts are credited as arriving in time.

For completeness, the distribution behind it - every lesion case in the pilot window that had *any* prior `NEDLAME`, by days from the most recent prior alert to the lesion:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lookback-rationale

lookback_gaps <- lame_lesion_recent |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event) |>
  distinct() |>
  left_join(nedlame_all, by = c("id_animal", "lact_number"),
            relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(!is.na(ned_date), ned_date < date_event) |>
  group_by(id_animal, lact_number, date_event) |>
  summarize(last_ned = max(ned_date), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(gap = as.numeric(date_event - last_ned),
         band = cut(gap, c(0, 7, 14, 21, 28, 45, 60, 90, Inf),
                    labels = c("0-7", "8-14", "15-21", "22-28",
                               "29-45", "46-60", "61-90", "90+"))) |>
  count(band, name = "cases")

lookback_gaps |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = band, values_from = cases) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Days from the last prior alert to the lesion",
             subtitle = paste0("n = ", sum(lookback_gaps$cases),
                               " lesion cases with any prior NEDLAME")) |>
  tab_source_note("The window is measured backward from the lesion only.")
```

The signal decays steeply - most alerts that precede a lesion do so within a week - and then runs out into a thin, flat tail. `r params$q4_lookback_days` days captures `r round(100 * sum(lookback_gaps$cases[lookback_gaps$band %in% c("0-7","8-14","15-21")]) / sum(lookback_gaps$cases))`% of all cases that had any prior alert. Extending to 28 days would add `r lookback_gaps$cases[lookback_gaps$band == "22-28"]` more.

The gap decays steeply - most alerts that precede a lesion do so within a week - and then runs out into a thin, flat tail with no structure in it.

**An earlier version of this report argued the window differently, and that argument does not hold.** It reported a second rise at 29-45 days and put the window in the trough before it. On the population the window actually governs - first diagnoses - there is no second rise. The bump is real, but it appears only when **repeat** lesions in the same lactation are counted: including them the 29-45 band holds 76 cases instead of `r lookback_gaps$cases[lookback_gaps$band == "29-45"]`.

Checking what those repeat cases are: **55% of them have a trim sitting between the alert and the lesion**, against 0% in the 0-14 day bands. So the bump is not the camera re-alerting after a trim, as was previously written - it is a cow whose alert was already acted on, who was trimmed, and whose *later* lesion is then being paired with that same old alert. Those cases are excluded from this report by the completed-cycle rule, so the bump is gone for a reason, not by luck.

Treat `r params$q4_lookback_days` days as **a defensible operational choice, not a natural constant.** Anything from roughly 14 to 45 days leaves the miss count untouched; what moves is the attribution within it.

A separate rule also applies: `lookback_days_used` is capped at how long `NEDLAME` had been live as of each lesion, so the window never reaches back before the system existed.

## What Lesions are being missed?

The figure below shows the lesion types found at all (cohort and non cohort cows) first-diagnosis cases, broken out by NEDAP detection status:

- **Alert Arrived in Time**
  - a `NEDLAME` landed in DairyComp inside the window before the lesion.
- **Alerted Earlier, No Trim Followed**
  - an alert arrived before the window opened and no trim happened in between.
- **Flagged, No Alert Raised**
  - the camera flagged her inside the window but no `NEDLAME` was raised. Mostly the enrollment rules declining the flag on purpose rather than anything going missing - see @fig-pipeline-loss-injury-plot.
- **Flagged Earlier, Outside the Window**
  - the camera did flag her, but only more than `r params$q4_lookback_days` days before the lesion - too far back to count as a warning about it.
- **No Flag Found**
  - no camera flag of any kind before the lesion.

Where a cow had two different lesions on the same day, each type is counted. The same type coded twice on one day counts once.

- **Panel A** asks how often each lesion is caught.

  - \% caught in time is listed inside the figure.

- **Panel B** asks what lesion each flag outcome tends to be, with *Alert Arrived in Time* as the comparison column

Lesion types with fewer than 20 cases are combined into one bar - separately they are too few to carry a percentage. Other is a combination category that holds lesions that were infrequent.

```{r}
#| label: fig-q4-lesion-types
#| fig-height: 9

invisible(list2env(fxn_build_q4_groups(q4_sensor, lame_lesion_recent), environment()))

STATUS_LEV <- c("Alert Arrived in Time", "Alerted Earlier, No Trim Followed",
                "Flagged, No Alert Raised", "Flagged Earlier, Outside the Window",
                "No Flag Found")

les_base <- q4_sensor |>
  filter(in_coverage) |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, detection_group_3way) |>
  mutate(status = factor(as.character(detection_group_3way), levels = STATUS_LEV))
# Same trap as elsewhere: a renamed level silently becomes NA and vanishes from
# every count while the page still renders. Assert the mapping caught everything.
stopifnot(!any(is.na(les_base$status)), nrow(les_base) > 0)

les_long <- lame_lesion_recent |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, all_of(lesion_type_cols)) |>
  inner_join(les_base |> select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, status),
             by = c("id_animal", "lact_number", "date_event")) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(lesion_type_cols), names_to = "lesion_type", values_to = "has_lesion") |>
  filter(has_lesion == 1)

# Types under 20 cases cannot carry a percentage: toe ulcer is 2 cows, and under
# the previous per-type chart those 2 rendered as a full-width 100% bar.
les_min_n  <- 20
les_tot    <- les_long |> count(lesion_type, name = "n_total")
les_rare   <- sort(les_tot$lesion_type[les_tot$n_total < les_min_n])
n_les_rare <- sum(les_tot$n_total[les_tot$n_total < les_min_n])
les_long   <- les_long |>
  mutate(lt = if_else(lesion_type %in% les_rare, "rare types (combined)", lesion_type))

n_by_lesion    <- les_long |> count(lt, name = "n_cases")
rate_by_lesion <- les_long |> count(lt, status) |>
  left_join(n_by_lesion, by = "lt") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / n_cases)

# Best to worst, left to right, by share caught in time.
les_ord <- rate_by_lesion |> filter(status == STATUS_LEV[1]) |>
  arrange(desc(pct)) |> pull(lt)
les_ord <- c(les_ord, setdiff(unique(les_long$lt), les_ord))
rate_by_lesion <- rate_by_lesion |> mutate(lt = factor(lt, levels = les_ord))
n_by_lesion    <- n_by_lesion    |> mutate(lt = factor(lt, levels = les_ord))

# Okabe-Ito, colourblind-safe, and deliberately NOT viridis: panel A uses viridis
# for STATUS, and two palettes both ending in yellow would make the lesion "dd"
# read as the status "Never Flagged".
les_pal <- setNames(c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#56B4E9", "#D55E00",
                      "#E69F00", "#999999")[seq_along(les_ord)], les_ord)

caught_lab <- rate_by_lesion |> filter(status == STATUS_LEV[1]) |>
  mutate(lab = paste0(round(pct), "%"))

# Best at the TOP: coord_flip() puts the first factor level at the bottom, so
# the display order is reversed here rather than in the ordering logic above.
rate_by_lesion <- rate_by_lesion |> mutate(lt = factor(lt, levels = rev(les_ord)))
n_by_lesion    <- n_by_lesion    |> mutate(lt = factor(lt, levels = rev(les_ord)))
caught_lab     <- caught_lab     |> mutate(lt = factor(lt, levels = rev(les_ord)))

p_lesion_rate <- ggplot(rate_by_lesion, aes(x = lt, y = pct, fill = fct_rev(status))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(data = caught_lab, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = lt, y = pct / 2, label = lab), colour = "white", size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(data = n_by_lesion, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = lt, y = 102, label = paste0("n=", n_cases)),
            hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     limits = c(0, 116), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(drop = FALSE, direction = -1,
                       guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE, nrow = 2)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of cases with that lesion", fill = NULL,
       title = "A. How often is each lesion caught?",
       ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = rev(les_pal[les_ord]), face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

n_by_status   <- les_base |> count(status, name = "n_cases")
mix_by_status <- les_long |> count(status, lt) |>
  left_join(n_by_status, by = "status") |>
  # rev() so that after coord_flip() the within-group order reads top-to-bottom
  # in the same order as the legend; guide_legend(reverse) keeps the two aligned.
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / n_cases, lt = factor(lt, levels = rev(les_ord)))

# Outcomes best-to-worst reading DOWN the axis. The previous vertical version
# claimed an order the reader could not see: the x-axis was ordered, but the eye
# went to the dodged bars inside each group, whose heights are not monotonic.
mix_by_status <- mix_by_status |>
  mutate(status = factor(as.character(status), levels = rev(STATUS_LEV)))
n_by_status   <- n_by_status   |>
  mutate(status = factor(as.character(status), levels = rev(STATUS_LEV)))

p_lesion_mix <- ggplot(mix_by_status, aes(x = status, y = pct, fill = lt)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.78, position = position_dodge(width = 0.85)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(pct)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.85),
            hjust = -0.25, size = 2.7, colour = "grey25") +
  geom_text(data = n_by_status, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = status, y = -4.5, label = paste0("n=", n_cases)),
            size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.10, 0.10))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = les_pal, guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2, reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) gsub(", ", ",\n", x)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of cases in that status", fill = NULL,
       title = "B. What lesion does each outcome tend to be?",
       subtitle = "Bars do not sum to 100% as a cow can have 1+ lesions.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

# Quoted in the prose below, so the text cannot drift from the figure.
pctl <- function(l, s) round(rate_by_lesion$pct[rate_by_lesion$lt == l & rate_by_lesion$status == s])
pctm <- function(l, s) round(mix_by_status$pct[mix_by_status$lt == l & mix_by_status$status == s])

p_lesion_rate / p_lesion_mix
```

- Digital dermatitis is the clear gap. The camera caught **`r pctl('dd', STATUS_LEV[1])`%** of DD cases in time against **`r pctl('wld', STATUS_LEV[1])`%** of white line

- DD is **`r pctm('dd', STATUS_LEV[5])`%** of the cases with no camera flag at all against **`r pctm('dd', STATUS_LEV[1])`%** of those where the alert arrived in time.

None of that is a surprise. Locomotion scoring is known to detect digital dermatitis poorly, and the camera is scoring locomotion, so a lesion that barely changes how a cow walks is the one it will tend to miss.

The `r length(les_rare)` lesion types with fewer than `r les_min_n` cases (`r paste(les_rare, collapse = ", ")`; `r n_les_rare` cases in total) are pooled into the "rare types (combined)" bar.

## Which leg is being missed?

Below is all lesions found by the trimmer split by which foot the lesion was found on and if it was alerted or not. A cow can have lesions on more than one foot, so the bars add to more than `r nrow(q4_group)` cases.

- Similar % for front vs rear so no clear pattern of the camera missing front feet.

```{r}
#| label: fig-missed-by-leg
#| fig-height: 4

leg_names <- c(LF = "Left Front", RF = "Right Front", LR = "Left Rear", RR = "Right Rear")

# locate_lesion packs one or more two-character foot codes into one string
# ("RRLR" = right rear + left rear, "RRLRRFLF" = all four). It must be parsed
# in 2-character chunks, NOT with substring matching: str_detect("LRRF", "RR")
# is TRUE, but "LRRF" is LR + RF, so substring matching would invent a
# right-rear lesion that was never recorded. Checked every value in the data -
# all are even length and every chunk is one of LF/RF/LR/RR.
leg_long <- events_formatted |>
  filter(event %in% c("LAME", "FOOTRIM", "TRIM"), !is.na(locate_lesion), locate_lesion != "") |>
  select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, locate_lesion) |>
  # locate_lesion packs one or more two-character foot codes into one string
  # ("RRLR" = right rear + left rear, "RRLRRFLF" = all four), so it must be
  # read in 2-character chunks, never by substring matching: str_detect("LRRF",
  # "RR") is TRUE but "LRRF" is LR + RF.
  #
  # It is built in functions/fxn_location.R, which used to search the whole
  # remark and so invented a phantom left front on XNLF* codes - XNL
  # (treatment) + F (foot rot) + RF (leg) is ONE foot, but "LF" spans the
  # treatment's trailing L and the lesion's F. Fixed at source, so nothing is
  # needed here.
  mutate(leg = str_extract_all(locate_lesion, ".{2}")) |>
  unnest(leg) |>
  filter(leg %in% names(leg_names)) |>
  distinct(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, leg) |>
  # Map to readable names HERE, once, so everything downstream sees
  # "Left Rear" rather than "LR". Leaving the raw codes in place and
  # renaming later silently broke a front/rear split that tested
  # str_detect(leg, "Rear") - it matched nothing and called every foot Front.
  mutate(leg = unname(leg_names[leg]))

q4_legs <- leg_long |>
  inner_join(q4_sensor |> select(id_animal, lact_number, date_event, detection_group_3way),
             by = c("id_animal", "lact_number", "date_event")) |>
  count(detection_group_3way, leg) |>
  # Same reasoning as the lesion-type figure above: a share within each foot,
  # so the four feet are comparable regardless of how many lesions each carries.
  group_by(leg) |>
  mutate(total_cases = sum(n), pct = 100 * n / total_cases) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(leg = fct_reorder(leg, total_cases))

leg_totals <- q4_legs |> distinct(leg, total_cases)

# leg is a factor now (ordered for the plot), and str_detect() rejects factors
n_legs_rear <- sum(q4_legs$n[str_detect(as.character(q4_legs$leg), "Rear")])
n_legs_front <- sum(q4_legs$n[str_detect(as.character(q4_legs$leg), "Front")])

ggplot(q4_legs, aes(x = leg, y = pct, fill = detection_group_3way)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = leg_totals, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = leg, y = 101, label = paste0("n=", total_cases)),
            hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     limits = c(0, 118), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE, nrow = 2)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of cases on that foot", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Was it a NEDAP Now problem?

Since we are running a separate SmartSight instance for NEDAP Now, I wanted to make sure all cows were visible on it. A cow absent from SmartSight is not being watched for lameness at all, so a lesion found on her cannot be a camera miss.

```{r}
#| label: platform-enrollment-build

q4_sensor <- q4_sensor |>
  left_join(events_all |> select(id_animal, id) |> distinct(), by = "id_animal") |>
  mutate(
    # alias-aware, matching the Q4 eligibility rule exactly - a cow enrolled
    # under a previous animal number is enrolled (see enrolled_ids in setup)
    not_in_smartsight = !(id %in% enrolled_ids),
    # Checked, not assumed: the point of this section is that a cow can be
    # current on the Activity platform (which staff use daily) while absent
    # from SmartSight. Earlier drafts asserted "even though she's on
    # Activity" in prose without computing it - now computed so the claim
    # can't drift away from the data.
    in_activity = id %in% cows_activity$id
  )

# Unenrolled cows are excluded upstream in Q4, so this should now be empty.
# Kept as an assertion rather than deleted: if it ever stops being zero, the
# exclusion has silently stopped working.
n_residual_not_in_smartsight <- sum(q4_sensor$is_miss & q4_sensor$not_in_smartsight)
n_total_misses <- sum(q4_sensor$is_miss)

# Herd-level enrollment check. The misses above are only the unenrolled cows
# who also happened to get a lesion, so they understate the gap. This asks the
# direct question instead: of every first-lactation cow that freshened in the
# study window, what share is on the SmartSight list at all? Compared against
# the Activity list, which is the control - if both dropped together it would
# point at the export; if only SmartSight drops it points at enrollment.
ss_ids  <- unique(cows_smartsight$id)
act_ids <- unique(cows_activity$id)

l1_fresh <- animal_lactations |>
  filter(lact_number == 1, !is.na(date_fresh), date_fresh >= ymd(params$history_after_date) - 150,
         date_fresh <= analysis_end) |>
  distinct(id_animal, id, date_fresh) |>
  mutate(id = as.character(id),
         on_smartsight = id %in% ss_ids,
         on_activity   = id %in% act_ids,
         fresh_month   = format(date_fresh, "%Y-%m"))

enroll_by_month <- l1_fresh |>
  group_by(`Freshened` = fresh_month) |>
  summarize(`Cows` = n(),
            `% on SmartSight` = round(100 * mean(on_smartsight), 1),
            `% on Activity`   = round(100 * mean(on_activity), 1),
            .groups = "drop")

# the hard break: the most recent freshening among enrolled first-lactation cows
last_enrolled_fresh <- max(l1_fresh$date_fresh[l1_fresh$on_smartsight], na.rm = TRUE)
l1_after  <- l1_fresh |> filter(date_fresh > last_enrolled_fresh)
l1_before <- l1_fresh |> filter(date_fresh <= last_enrolled_fresh)
n_l1_after_unenrolled <- sum(!l1_after$on_smartsight)
pct_l1_before_enrolled <- round(100 * mean(l1_before$on_smartsight), 1)
n_l1_after_on_activity <- sum(l1_after$on_activity)

```

- `r n_excluded_not_enrolled` lesion cases were excluded on this basis, and they are no longer counted as misses anywhere above.

- Digging further showed that

  - The most recent freshening among first-lactation cows who *are* on SmartSight was **`r format(last_enrolled_fresh)`**.

  - After that date **`r n_l1_after_unenrolled` first-lactation cows are absent** in the SmartSight instance.


## Why Did No Alert Arrive in Time?

Due to the DairyComp and data entry set up there are several ways a cow that is flagged would not have a NEDAP Lame event (see @fig-pipeline-loss-injury-plot)

- A low score \<31 but recently trimmed or flagged

  - `r n_only_ftdat` had every flag land inside its own `FTDAT` window (90 days for `Low`, 28 for the declines).

- A low score and an injury event

  - `r n_only_injury` had a history of upper-leg lameness (`Leg-AboveFoot`), which blocks the `Low` route.

- Cow flagged after trim data but trim data was entered retrospectively.

  - `r n_only_late` did get an alert, but it arrived a day after the lesion was recorded.

That accounts for **`r n_pipeline_loss_by_design` of the `r nrow(pipeline_loss_cases)`**. The remaining `r n_pipeline_loss_unexplained` are not explained by any of those rules - but they are not all failures either, and the split matters:

- **`r n_pipeline_loss_unknowable` cannot be judged at all.** Only a `LOW` flag fired, and the `Low` route requires a score of 1-30. Score-at-flag is not in this data, so a cow scoring 31-69 who was correctly declined looks exactly like a lost flag.

- **`r n_pipeline_loss_genuine` are genuine pipeline losses.** A decline route fired, and the decline routes carry no score gate.

  - Since we don't have the actual files that were filed in it is unclear if those cows made it to that stage.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pipeline-loss-injury-plot
#| fig-height: 4

# `reason` assigns ONE cause per case, so these bars sum to the total and
# match the counts in the prose. They used to be computed separately here.
pipeline_loss_cases |>
  count(category = reason) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(category, n), y = n, fill = category)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "N Cases") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)))
```

## Of the Misses, Did Farm Staff Catch Them Anyway?

```{r}
#| label: q4-staff-catch-build

invisible(list2env(fxn_build_staff_catch(q4, chklame), environment()))
```

Of the `r nrow(staff_catch)` cows whose lesion had no `NEDLAME` alert recorded in DairyComp beforehand (they were trimmed by routine trimming or because staff picked them out),

- `r sum(staff_catch$staff_flagged)` (`r round(100 * mean(staff_catch$staff_flagged), 1)`%) were flagged by the farm staff in the 7 days before diagnosis.
